record.title: Characterization of the set of 3-local profiles of large graphs
record.statement: For a graph $G$ and $i\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $p_i(G)$ be the probability that three distinct vertices chosen uniformly at random from $G$ span exactly $i$ edges, and write $p(G)=(p_0(G),p_1(G),p_2(G),p_3(G))$. Let $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^4$ be the set of all limit points of sequences $p(G_n)$, where $|V(G_n)|\to\infty$. Describe the set $S$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/02](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12330), page 42. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Equality of the SPN solutions for two planar screen descriptions
record.statement: For the Cantor-screen construction described in the report, the variational-formulation solutions satisfy $u_2=u_3$ for every incident field (1) if and only if $\alpha\ge 4$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/03](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12331), page 29. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Tractability of numerical integration for infinitely differentiable functions
record.statement: Consider the class $F_d=\{f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb{R}\mid \|D^\alpha f\|_\infty\le 1\text{ for all }\alpha\in\mathbb{N}_0^d\}$ and the numerical integration problem $S_d(f)=\int_{[0,1]^d}f(x)\,dx$. Is this problem tractable? Does it suffer from the curse of dimensionality?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/04](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12332), page 30. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Positivity and the inverse Klain map
record.statement: Assume that $K$ is a centrally symmetric convex body. Then $K\in K(i)$ if and only if $\varphi(K)\ge 0$ for every even, $i$-homogeneous, continuous, translation-invariant valuation $\varphi$ with nonnegative Klain function.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/05](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12333), page 25. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Artin’s conjecture for supersingular K3 surfaces
record.statement: For a K3 surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, if the height $h$ of its formal Brauer group is $\infty$, then its Picard number satisfies $\rho=22$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/06](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12334), page 12. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Higher-dimensional regularity of the nonlinear gradient field for p-harmonic functions
record.statement:
Conjecture: For every dimension $n\ge 3$, every $p\in(1,\infty)$, and every scalar $p$-harmonic function $u$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, the field
\[
V(\nabla u):=|\nabla u|^{(p-2)/2}\nabla u
\]
belongs to $C^1$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/08](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12336), page 45. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Two-dimensional dispersive estimate for the Coriolis linear group
record.statement:
For all $t\ge 0$, $\Omega\in\mathbb{R}$, and $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^3)$ satisfying
\[
\operatorname{supp}\widehat f\subset\left\{\xi\in\mathbb{R}^3:\frac12\le |\xi|\le 2\right\},
\]
there exists a constant $C$ such that
\[
\left\|e^{\pm i\Omega t D_3/|D|}f\right\|_{L^\infty}\le C(1+|\Omega|t)^{-1}\|f\|_{L^1}.
\]
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/10](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12338), page 8. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Finite-time blow-up for the inviscid primitive equations
record.statement: There exists smooth initial data for which the corresponding smooth solution of equations (6)–(10)—the three-dimensional inviscid primitive equations without Coriolis force, in the horizontal channel with the stated boundary conditions—blows up in finite time.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/10](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12338), page 19. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Gaussian Gabor-frame conjecture for the lattice \913\
record.statement:
Let $g(t)=2^{d/4}e^{-\c0 t\b7t/2}$ be the normalized Gaussian, and let $\Lambda_3=A_3(\mathbb Z+i\mathbb Z)^2\subset\mathbb C^2\cong\mathbb R^4$, where
\[
A_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&\frac25\\[2pt]0&\frac{\sqrt{21}}5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then the conjecture is that the Gabor system $G(g,\Lambda_3)=\{\pi(\lambda)g:\lambda\in\Lambda_3\}$ is a frame for $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/11](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12339), page 16. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Optimality of the Plateau-type upper bound for the triple-junction map
record.statement: For the triple-junction map $u$ taking the three vertices of an equilateral triangle as values on three sectors of the source plane meeting at $120^\circ$ angles, is the upper bound for the relaxed graph area $A(u,\Omega)$ obtained by the construction in [2] equal to the actual value $A(u,\Omega)$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/15](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12343), page 13. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Sidorenko’s conjecture for bipartite graphs
record.statement:
For every bipartite graph $F$ and every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with at least $\rho n^2/2$ edges, the number of homomorphisms from $F$ to $G$ satisfies
\[
t(F,G)\ge \rho^{e_F}n^{v_F},
\]
where $v_F=|V(F)|$ and $e_F=|E(F)|$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12479), page 21. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Nathan Linial’s signing conjecture
record.statement: For every d-regular graph \(G\), it is always possible to put values \(\pm1\) on the edges such that all eigenvalues of the obtained signed matrix lie in the interval \([ -2\sqrt{d-1},\,2\sqrt{d-1} ]\).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12479), page 36. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Margulis’ uniform-discreteness conjecture
record.statement: Margulis conjectured that the family of all cocompact torsion-free arithmetic lattices in $G$ is uniformly discrete.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/16](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12479), page 40. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Positivity in T-equivariant K-theory of flag varieties associated to Kac–Moody groups
record.statement: Let $G$ be a symmetrizable Kac–Moody group, let $W$ be its Weyl group, and let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r$ be the simple roots. If $p^w_{u,v}\in R(T)$ are defined by the product $\psi_u\cdot\psi_v=\sum_{w\in W}p^w_{u,v}\psi_w$ in $K_T^{\mathrm{top}}(X)$, then, for every $u,v,w\in W$, $$(-1)^{\ell(u)+\ell(v)+\ell(w)}p^w_{u,v}\in\mathbb Z_+[(e^{-\alpha_1}-1),\ldots,(e^{-\alpha_r}-1)].$$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12480), page 17. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Canonical dimension of anisotropic algebraic tori
record.statement: Is $\operatorname{cdim}(T)=\dim T$ for every anisotropic algebraic torus $T$ split by a Galois extension of prime-power degree?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12480), page 24. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Soergel's conjecture on indecomposable Soergel bimodules
record.statement: Soergel conjectured that the basis of the Hecke algebra given by indecomposable Soergel bimodules categorifies the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis; the report states that Elias and Williamson deduce this conjecture, and hence the Kazhdan–Lusztig positivity conjecture, for arbitrary Coxeter groups.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/17](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12480), page 54. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Existence of the limiting normalized number of $k$-colorings
record.statement:
For every integer $k\ge 3$ and every real $d>0$, the limit
\[
\varphi(d)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb{E}\left[\sqrt[n]{\#\{\text{$k$-colorings of }G(n,m)\}}\right]
\]
exists, where $G(n,m)$ is the random-graph model at average degree $d$ as specified in the report.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/18](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12481), page 13. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Theorem 4: counting labeled $G$-free graphs with $m$ edges
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $2$-balanced graph and let $\delta$ be a positive constant. There exists a constant $C$ such that for every $n
aq\in\mathbb{N}$, if $m\ge Cn^{2-1/m_2(G)}$, then
$$\binom{\operatorname{ex}(n,G)}{m}\le f_{n,m}(G)\le \binom{\operatorname{ex}(n,G)+\delta n^2}{m}.$$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/18](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12481), page 26. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Linear edge bound for fixed-t-quasi-planar topological graphs
record.statement: For every integer $t\ge 2$, there is a constant $c_t$ such that every $t$-quasi-planar topological graph on $n$ vertices has at most $c_t n$ edges, where a topological graph is drawn in the plane with vertices represented by points and edges by curves joining their corresponding endpoints, and $t$-quasi-planar means that it has no $t$ pairwise crossing edges.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/18](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12481), page 56. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Homomorphism and chromatic thresholds of clique-free graphs
record.statement:
For every integer $r \ge 3$, the homomorphism and chromatic thresholds of $K_r$ satisfy
\[
\delta_{K_r,\mathrm{hom}}=\delta_{K_r,\chi}=\frac{2r-5}{2r-3}.
\]
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/18](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12481), page 59. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Gromov–Hausdorff scaling limit of the dual tree of a recursive triangulation
record.statement: Let $\beta=(\sqrt{17}-3)/2$, let $T_n$ be the dual tree of the recursive triangulation at time $n$, equipped with its graph distance, and let $T_M$ be the compact real tree encoded by the random continuous process $M$ described in the report. The conjecture is that, as $n\to\infty$, the rescaled metric space $n^{-\beta/2}T_n$ converges to $T_M$ in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/20](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12483), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Existence and regularity of Willmore minimizers in arbitrary torus conformal classes
record.statement: For every conformal class of a torus, is the infimum of the Willmore energy attained by a smooth minimizer, without assuming that the infimum in that conformal class is below $8\pi$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/21](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12484), page 22. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Stable component count for Hurwitz spaces over curves of arbitrary genus
record.statement: For each equipped finite group $(G,O)$, where $O=C_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup C_m$ and the elements of $O$ generate $G$, there is a constant $T$ such that, for any projective irreducible nonsingular curve $F$, the number of irreducible components of every non-empty Hurwitz space $\operatorname{HUR}_{d,G,\tau}(F)$ equals $a(G,O)$ whenever $\tau_i\ge T$ for all $i=1,\ldots,m$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/27](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12490), page 34. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Exceptional sequence and quasi-phantom component for the classical Godeaux surface
record.statement: Let $Y=\{x_1^5+x_2^5+x_3^5+x_4^5=0\}\subset \mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{C}}$ and let $G=\mathbb{Z}/5=\langle\xi\rangle$ act by $x_i\mapsto \xi^i x_i$. For the classical Godeaux surface $X=Y/G$, there exists a semiorthogonal decomposition $D^b(X)=\langle A,L_1,\ldots,L_{11}\rangle$, where $L_i\in\operatorname{Pic}(X)$ and $A$ is non-trivial with $HH^\bullet(A)=0$ and $K_0(A)=\mathbb{Z}/5$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/27](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12490), page 52. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Abstract simplicity of irreducible complete Kac–Moody groups over arbitrary fields
record.statement: Is every irreducible complete Kac–Moody group $G(k)$ over an arbitrary field $k$ abstractly simple?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12491), page 33. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Every finite group is involved in a mapping class group
record.statement: Let \(\Sigma_g\) be a closed orientable surface of genus \(g\ge 1\), and let \(\Gamma_g\) be its orientation-preserving mapping class group. A group \(H\) is involved in a group \(G\) if there is a finite-index subgroup \(K<G\) admitting an epimorphism onto \(H\). Then, for all \(g\ge 1\), every finite group is involved in \(\Gamma_g\).
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12491), page 37. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: CAT(0) conjecture for all braid groups
record.statement: For all integers $n$, the $n$-strand braid group $B_n$ is CAT$(0)$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/28](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12491), page 39. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Unconditional lower bound for higher Pythagoras numbers
record.statement:
Show unconditionally that, for every real function field $F/K$ in $d$ variables and every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, the higher Pythagoras number satisfies
\[
p_{2m}(F)\ge d+1.
\]
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/30](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12493), page 43. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Grothendieck–Serre conjecture for reductive group schemes
record.statement: Let $R$ be a regular local ring, let $K$ be its field of fractions, and let $G$ be a reductive group scheme over $R$. Then the map $H^1_{\00\acute{\mathrm{e}t}}(R,G) \to H^1_{\acute{\mathrm{e}t}}(K,G)$ induced by the inclusion $R\hookrightarrow K$ has trivial kernel.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/31](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12494), page 28. Canonicalized from 9 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Factorization of motivic Hopf maps through Milnor–Witt K-theory modulo 24
record.statement:
For any integer $n\ge 3$, the morphism $(\nu_n)_*$ factors through a morphism
$$\mathbf K^{MW}_{n+2}/24\longrightarrow \pi^{\mathbb A^1}_{n+1}(\mathbb P^1\wedge n).$$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/32](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12495), page 34. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Diameter growth for long-time 3-dimensional Ricci flows on a single geometric piece
record.statement: Is the diameter of the manifold bounded by $C\sqrt{t}$ for all sufficiently large $t$ whenever the underlying manifold consists of a single geometric piece?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/33](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12581), page 10. Canonicalized from 4 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Finiteness of surgeries in Perelman’s Ricci flow
record.statement: There is a continuous function $\delta:[0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ such that the following holds: Let $M$ be a Ricci flow with surgery with normalized initial conditions which is performed by at least $\delta(t)$-precise cutoff. Then $M$ has only finitely many surgeries, and there are constants $T,C<\infty$ such that $|\mathrm{Rm}_t|<Ct^{-1}$ on $M(t)$ for all $t\ge T$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/33](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12581), page 10. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Bourgain’s subpolynomial-growth conjecture for cubic defocusing NLS
record.statement: For the periodic cubic defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation (0.1) with convolution potential $V=0$ in dimension $2$ or higher, Bourgain conjectured that the growth of the $H^s$ norm, for $s>1$, should be subpolynomial in time: $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\ll t^{\varepsilon}\|u(0)\|_{H^s}$ as $t\to\infty$, for every $\varepsilon>0$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/34](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12582), page 25. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Tits alternative for real-analytic area-preserving surface diffeomorphisms
record.statement: **Conjecture 15 (Tits alternative).** If $M$ is a compact surface, then every finitely generated subgroup of $\operatorname{Symp}^{\omega}_{\mu}(M)$ is either virtually solvable or contains a non-abelian free group.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/34](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12582), page 55. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Serre’s uniformity problem for elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$
record.statement: Does there exist a positive number $p_0$ such that, for every elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ without complex multiplication and every prime number $p>p_0$, the Galois representation $\rho_{E,p}:\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})\to \operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$ is surjective?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12583), page 8. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Boyd’s Mahler-measure identity for the conductor-15 elliptic curve
record.statement:
For the elliptic curve $E$ defined by $x+x^{-1}+y+y^{-1}+1=0$ (of conductor $15$),
\[
m\!\left(x+x^{-1}+y+y^{-1}+1\right)=\frac{15}{4\pi^{2}}L(E,2).
\]
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12583), page 21. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Absolute abelian Galois groups of imaginary quadratic fields with prime class number
record.statement: Based on numerical calculations, we conjecture that for 100% of all imaginary quadratic fields of prime class number, the absolute abelian Galois group is in fact isomorphic to $A_0$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12583), page 26. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Square-summability for Szegő-class Jacobi matrices
record.statement:
Let $E$ be the fixed Parreau–Widom set, let $J' = \{a'_n,b'_n\}_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}\in \mathcal{T}_E$, and let $J = \{a_n,b_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be an arbitrary Jacobi matrix. If $J$ lies in the Szegő class for $E$ and $\chi(J)=\chi(J')$, then

$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left((a_n-a'_n)^2+(b_n-b'_n)^2\right)<\infty.$$
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/36](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12584), page 6. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Conjecture 1: ℓ¹ perturbations and the Szegő class
record.statement:
Suppose $J' = \{a'_n,b'_n\}_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}$ belongs to $T_E$, and let $J = \{a_n,b_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be an arbitrary Jacobi matrix. If
$$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(|a_n-a'_n|+|b_n-b'_n|\right)<\infty,$$
then $J$ belongs to the Szegő class for $E$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/36](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12584), page 8. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Dynamical stability of compact Ricci-flat metrics
record.statement: Let $(M,\hat g)$ be a compact Ricci-flat manifold. If $\hat g$ is a local maximizer of Perelman’s $\lambda$-functional, then for every $C^{k,\alpha}$-neighborhood $U$ of $\hat g$, with $k\ge 2$, there exists a $C^{k,\alpha}$-neighborhood $V\subset U$ such that the Ricci flow starting at any metric in $V$ exists for all times and converges, modulo diffeomorphisms, to a Ricci-flat metric in $U$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/37](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12585), page 13. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Theorem 2: Smoothness under vanishing residues at a branch point
record.statement: For the constrained Willmore immersion considered in the report, suppose that both residues at the origin—the second residue $\beta$ and the first-residue vector $\vec{\beta}_0$—vanish. Then: (i) if $\theta_0<\mu+2$, the immersion is smooth across the branch point; (ii) if $\theta_0=\mu+2$, the immersion is of class $C^{\theta_0+1,1-\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/37](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12585), page 23. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Willmore conjecture for immersed tori in Euclidean three-space
record.statement: For every torus immersed in Euclidean three-space, the integral of the square of its mean curvature is at least $2\pi^2$. In the report’s convention, this is $W(\Phi)=\int_{T^2}|\vec H|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}_g\ge 2\pi^2$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/37](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12585), page 33. Canonicalized from 3 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Positive solutions of the supercritical Lane–Emden equation on topologically nontrivial domains
record.statement:
Is it true that, for every smoothly bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge 3$ and nontrivial topology—in particular, for domains sufficiently close to an annulus—the Dirichlet problem
\[
-\Delta u=|u|^{p-2}u\quad\text{in }\Omega,\qquad u=0\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega,
\]
has a solution satisfying $u>0$ for every $p>2$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/40](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12588), page 48. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Margulis’s uniform-discreteness conjecture for arithmetic uniform lattices
record.statement: For every fixed semisimple Lie group $G$, the family of all torsion-free arithmetic uniform lattices in $G$ is uniformly discrete; equivalently, the minimal injectivity radii of the associated locally symmetric manifolds have a common positive lower bound.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/42](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12590), page 8. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Limit multiplicity for arbitrary finite-index subgroups without central elements
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be an irreducible arithmetic lattice. Does the limit multiplicity property hold for every collection $\mathcal D$ of finite-index subgroups $\Delta\leq\Gamma$ such that no $\Delta\in\mathcal D$ contains a non-trivial central element?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/42](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12590), page 34. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Limit multiplicity for subgroups of irreducible arithmetic lattices

record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/42](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12590), page 34. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Strong finite embeddability of countable discrete groups into Hilbert space
record.statement: Is every countable discrete group $\Gamma$ strongly finitely embeddable into a Hilbert space $H$? Here, strong finite embeddability means that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_n\in\operatorname{Aut}(\Gamma)$, the semidirect product $\Gamma\rtimes_{\{\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_n\}}F_n$ is finitely embeddable into $H$.

record.title: Invariant subspace problem for separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces (version I)

record.title: Invariant subspace problem relative to a von Neumann algebra
record.statement: Let $H$ be an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space. Is there, for arbitrary $T\in B(H)\setminus \mathbb{C}I$, a projection $p$ belonging to the von Neumann algebra generated by $T$ such that $p\notin\{0,1\}$ and $Tp=pTp$?
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/45](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12593), page 67. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

record.title: Small ball conjecture for hyperbolic sums of multiparameter Haar functions
record.statement:
For dimensions $d\ge 3$, it is conjectured that, for all relevant integers $n$ and arbitrary real coefficients $\alpha_R$,
\[
n^{(d-2)/2}\left\lVert\sum_{|R|=2^{-n}}\alpha_R h_R\right\rVert_{L^\infty([0,1]^d)}\gtrsim 2^{-n}\sum_{|R|=2^{-n}}|\alpha_R|,
\]
where $h_R$ is an $L^\infty$-normalized $d$-dimensional Haar function adapted to the dyadic rectangle $R\subset[0,1]^d$.
record.references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/49](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12723), page 8. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.
